title: Interviews on Mindful Birding
description: The feeling of birding is for everyone, but not everyone experiences birds the same way. Interviewed blind/low vision and novice sighted birders to understand how they engage with birding-by-ear experiences and reminisce about bird sounds.
researcher: Katarina Blind, Catherine Fu, Jax Powell
summary: Conducted interviews with blind/low-vision and sighted birders. Key findings: people share birding media socially to relive moments but rarely revisit recordings; people want low-commitment ways to learn about birds; audio-first experiences are most accessible.
tags: auditory-first birding,mindful birding,blind birders,low vision birders,novice birders,qualitative
key_findings: People reminisce by sharing birding media. People rarely revisit past recordings alone. Want low-commitment bird learning. Birding-by-ear is most accessible to all abilities.

title: Field Observations with Blind and Novice Birders
description: Observed group of novice birders and separately a group of blind birders to understand how they bird and note behavioral data. Objective: bring mindful birding experience from VI community to all birders of all abilities.
researcher: Katarina Blind, Catherine Fu, Jax Powell
summary: Conducted observations with novice and blind birders in natural settings. Findings: birding is fundamentally about listening and mindfulness; blind birders redefine birding; technology and community support learning and connection; Merlin Bird ID commonly used.
tags: auditory-first birding,mindful birding,blind birders,novice birders,field observations,observational
key_findings: Birding is fundamentally about listening and mindfulness. Blind birders redefine birding. Technology and community support learning. Merlin Bird ID widely adopted.

title: Mixed Visual Ability Co-design Sessions
description: Collaborative design sessions with blind/low-vision and novice sighted birders. Co-designed solutions for accessible and engaging birding experiences.
researcher: Katarina Blind, Catherine Fu, Jax Powell
summary: Co-design workshops with mixed visual abilities exploring accessible birding design solutions. Participants focused on: audio documentation, sharing mechanisms, and community features for reminiscing about birding experiences.
key_findings: Participants want accessible audio documentation tools. Sharing mechanisms increase engagement. Community features support bird learning. Peer support is valued.

title: App Review Analysis
description: Analysis of user reviews and feedback from app stores and community platforms to understand user sentiment, pain points, and feature requests.
researcher: Katarina Blind, Catherine Fu, Jax Powell
summary: Analyzed app reviews to understand user sentiment and feature requests. Reviewed trends in user feedback across accessibility, features, and community engagement.
tags: desk research,quantitative,app store reviews,user feedback,content analysis
key_findings: Key themes from reviews: accessibility features highly valued. Users want better documentation and tutorials. Community features drive engagement.

title: Merlin Instagram Analysis
description: Analysis of Merlin's Instagram community engagement, followers, content themes, and audience interaction patterns to understand community sentiment and content preferences.
researcher: Katarina Blind, Catherine Fu, Jax Powell
summary: Analyzed Merlin Instagram data for community engagement patterns. Findings: user-generated content drives highest engagement; audio and visual content equally valued; community shares experiences and bird identifications.
key_findings: User-generated content drives engagement. Birds are shared for identification and reminiscence. Community is active and supportive. Audio and visual content both valuable.

title: Social Media Desk Ticket Analysis
description: Analysis of support tickets and user-reported issues from social media channels to identify common problems and user needs.
researcher: Katarina Blind, Catherine Fu, Jax Powell
summary: Analyzed support tickets from social media for common issues and user pain points. Findings: accessibility issues are frequent; users need better tutorials; feature requests cluster around documentation and sharing.
key_findings: Accessibility issues frequently reported. Users struggle with app features without documentation. Sharing features highly requested. Community support is critical.

title: Iterative Prototype Testing
description: Multiple rounds of prototype testing with users to refine design based on feedback. Evaluated early-stage prototypes for accessibility and usability.
researcher: Katarina Blind, Catherine Fu, Jax Powell
summary: Conducted iterative rounds of prototype testing with blind and sighted users. Testing focused on: audio interface usability, documentation clarity, and sharing features. Refined designs based on direct feedback.
key_findings: Audio interface improved through testing. Users need clearer onboarding. Sharing workflow needs simplification. Accessibility features are essential.

title: Formal Prototype Testing
description: Formal usability testing sessions with structured protocol evaluating prototype features for accessibility, learnability, and engagement.
researcher: Katarina Blind, Catherine Fu, Jax Powell
summary: Conducted formal usability testing of prototype features. Protocol evaluated: audio interface quality, feature discoverability, accessibility compliance, and user satisfaction. Collected quantitative metrics and qualitative feedback.
key_findings: Audio quality and clarity critical for success. Users need guided onboarding. Accessibility features work well but need visibility. Feature discoverability needs improvement.
